statements.t: Customer commitments are in line with our full-year sales plans, and uncommitted tobacco inventories are within our target range.
We forecast shipments to be heavily weighted to the second half of our fiscal year 2027, consistent with our plans and with historical patterns.
We also expect uncommitted inventories to reduce further during that period.
Together, these factors give us confidence in our outlook for the balance of the fiscal year.
We are transforming our platform into a more integrated and aligned organization, a process we expect to continue through our fiscal year 2028.
While market and cost pressures remain, we are confident in our strategy, and we believe the actions underway will strengthen the business and its contribution to Universal over time.

U niversal continues to deepen its collaboration with customers on the sustainability priorities shaping the leaf tobacco supply chain, empowering our teams on the ground to deliver projects that are impactful to farming communities.
We will continue to build on this work in close partnership with our customers.
Universal expects to publish its fiscal year 2026 Sustainability Report in early December, which will further detail our significant supply chain activities.
We expect fiscal year 2027 tobacco shipments to be heavily weighted to the second half of the fiscal year.
As a result, we expect to recover more of our working capital investments later in fiscal year 2027 than in fiscal year 2026.
We generally do not purchase material quantities of tobacco on a speculative basis, and we target committed inventory levels of 80% or more of total tobacco inventory.
We expect our uncommitted tobacco inventory levels to come down from September 30, 2026 levels in the second half of fiscal year 2027.
Typically, our capital expenditures for maintenance projects are less than $30 million per fiscal year.

In addition, from time to time, we undertake projects that require capital expenditures when we identify opportunities to improve efficiencies, invest in sustainability projects, add value for our customers, and position ourselves for future growth.

We currently expect to spend approximately $60 to $70 million over the next twelve months on capital projects for maintenance of our facilities and other investments to grow and improve our businesses.

We also use derivative instruments from time to time to hedge certain foreign currency exposures, primarily related to forecasted purchases of tobacco, related processing costs, and crop input sales, as well as our net monetary balance sheet exposures in local currency.
We generally account for our hedges of forecasted tobacco purchases as cash flow hedges.
As of September 30, 2026, the fair value of our open hedges for forecasted tobacco purchases and crop inputs was a net asset of approximately $63 thousand.
